shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares, using the anchor name of the node that owns the thing (envelope and cas from N-01, record-kinds-registry from N-18, codes from N-43, break-glass from N-27). check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for alerts.rendered 200; alert.acked 201; alert.ack-conflict 409; alert.aged 410; alerts.invalid 422; alerts.stale 503; alerts.view-timeout 504. Owner-acts: alert.aged (one card).
A lamp column per code (green, amber or red) so a screen draws a code without a table of its own; N-37 generates bindings from it and the alert strip colour and every row chip read it.

An escalation_bound_s column per owner-acts code (default 86400): the N-31 tick compares every open alert against it each minute and escalates once to 410 alert.aged with one card, so an alert never waits on a person without a bound.
The acts column (system, owner, seat, nobody): a code whose acts is owner is an alert row by property of the code; no node and no agent raises an alert by hand.
The record envelope every kind carries: id, at (UTC), code, kind, node, attempt where one applies; this node reads and writes records only inside it.
Compare-and-swap: expected_version on an entity write; 409 with the current version on a miss; expected 0 inserts.
entities(key, version, body, updated_at): an open alert is an entity keyed by its source record id; its version is what an alert.ack compares and swaps on.
idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response with code 200.

The record kinds registry (every kind with its code set, writer node and schema path, loaded by N-43 with the code table) carries the kinds this node reads and writes: alert (keyed by source record id), alert.ack, stall (N-12), dead (N-11), merge.hold (N-10), health (N-06), card (N-28).
A stall record (run killed, lease revoked, reason) is one alert row; the row names the reason and the attempt the system took next.
Cards are idempotent by source id, so an alert that is also a card never posts twice and the ack on the page closes both.
No cog: every wait has a timeout and a fallback, nothing starts by an agent typing, no agent is a gate; the system drives (brief C rule 3).
Many agents at once from the first line: append-only records, compare-and-swap, idempotent retryable steps, conflicts that report as 409 (brief C rule 2).
Every automated step retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers and reports as a record; a dead record becomes exactly one card.
The owner's always-on monitor never stops on a halt; a HOLD dims actions, never the screens (brief C, command center volume).

purpose.s: Every red and amber lamp in one list, newest first: the alert code from the status code map, the node, since (UTC), the cause line, the retry count, and what the system already did about it (wireframe-brief.json screen Alerts; C32 approved). Primary action: jump to the machine.

The owner's job on this screen: find out why a machine is red and what the system already did; acknowledge an alert so it stops shouting while the system keeps working on it. Acknowledging never resolves: an alert resolves only on a later 2xx record whose recovery_of names that alert (record.schema.json#/$defs/recovery_of), written by the system; an unrelated 2xx on the same node and ticket resolves nothing.

input.s: An alert is a record whose status code the code table marks as alerting (red or amber lamp): stall (N-12, 410), dead (N-11, after three attempts), rejected main (N-10, 422 with merge.hold), unhealthy (N-06 health), plus the map group's own alerting codes (deploy 5xx, art 422, binding 422, frame 422). N-31 pushes alert records and, for each, the attempt and resolution records that follow, so "what the system did" is a join the server makes, never a text a seat writes.

Each alert carries: id, code, node, ticket (with full title), since, cause (the record's message), retries so far (N-11 attempt), system_did (the latest attempt or recovery record one-liner), card_id when N-28 posted a card for it, resolved_at and resolved_by_record when a 2xx naming it in recovery_of closed it, acked (by, at, version).

output.s: alerts.frame is the drawn list; not stored. The store write is the alert.ack record: alert id, owner, at UTC, the alert version the ack was made against (compare-and-swap), and the client's idempotency key. A tap on a row writes a selection record (N-38's shape, source alerts) and opens the Machine screen.

panels.panel: Title Alerts, newest first, times in UTC; segment filter All, Red, Amber with counts; a node filter chip when opened from a machine.
One row per open alert: lamp, code, node, since and age, cause, retries, what the system did, Open machine button; acked rows dimmed with the ack time; a card chip when a card is open for it.
Resolved in the last 7 days, collapsed, count shown; Show resolved expands.
Lamp key from the code table and the reading hint: tap a row to jump to its machine.
The Acknowledge control on a row (owner key only) and its result: acknowledged, already acknowledged by, or not recorded with the queued indicator.

mechanism.diagram: flowchart LR R10[N-10 rejected main] --> ST[N-01 store: alerting codes] R11[N-11 dead, attempt n+1] --> ST R12[N-12 stall] --> ST R06[N-06 unhealthy] --> ST ST --> J[N-31: alert view, joined with attempts, cards, recovery_of] J --> C[client: alerts module] C --> D[alerts.frame drawn newest first] C -->|Acknowledge, owner key| A[alert.ack: CAS on alert version] A -->|201| C A -->|200 replay of the same send| C A -->|409 already acked or changed| C REC[any 2xx with recovery_of = alert id] --> ST C -->|tap a row| SEL[selection record, source alerts] --> M[N-39]

step.s: Alerting is a property of the code, not of a node: the code table (N-43) carries lamp red or amber and acts owner or system for every code; the alert view selects records with an alerting code and no later 2xx record whose recovery_of names them. Nothing is "raised" by a separate call, so a node cannot forget to alert (the board froze six hours and nobody raised anything, L08 section 5).

The join: for each alert, the latest N-11 attempt record on the same ticket gives retries and system_did; the N-28 card record with the same source id gives card_id; the 2xx record whose recovery_of equals the alert id gives resolved_at and resolved_by_record. The view is pushed as deltas keyed by alert id and version.

Rows render newest first; the filter is local; the node filter comes from the deep link /board#alerts/N-xx the Machine screen uses. Acknowledge is shown only on the owner key; it sends alert.ack with the alert's current version; the server applies compare-and-swap on that version: 201 when it matches, 409 when the alert changed or is already acked, with the acker and time in the reply.

An ack dims the row and stops the alert chip counting it on the Map; it does not change the lamp on the machine (the machine is still red until the system writes a 2xx), so the owner never silences a real fault.

Cards: N-28 builds exactly one card for a code that maps to owner-acts; the Alerts row shows the card chip and links to the card on the bearings page; answering the card is N-29's traversal, never this screen's.

states.state: Four open alerts at realistic volume (three red, one amber), one with a longest-plausible cause line, 31 resolved collapsed.
No open alert: the empty block with the explanation (every lamp is green or grey) and the primary recovery action as a real button: Open the map.
Skeleton rows matching the table shape; no centred spinner.
not-found (the alert view is absent), timeout (no frame within 10 s), validation (frame failed schema); what to do next and Retry.
Last list stays with the as-of stamp; Acknowledge taps queue with the indicator and send on reconnect with their original version (a changed alert yields 409 and the row shows it).

start.s: Alerts exist as soon as a record with an alerting code lands; the view is pushed; the client subscribes on open. Ships in the N-38 bundle, promoted by N-48. No agent raises, lists or clears an alert by hand.

wait.name: alert-view-first-frame
wait.fallback: error state class timeout with Retry; automatic retry continues
wait.s: From the subscription to the first alert view.

wait.name: alert-view-staleness
wait.fallback: stale chip (503); at 60 s offline banner; last list stays
wait.s: Deltas or the idle heartbeat at least every 5 s.

wait.name: ack-reply
wait.fallback: resend with the same idempotency key and version up to 3 times; then queued indicator and resend on reconnect; never a silent drop
wait.s: From the ack send to the 201 or 409 reply.

wait.name: resolution
wait.fallback: an open alert older than its escalation bound raises its own alert code 410 alert.aged on N-28 so one card is built; no repeat card
wait.s: An alert stays open until the system writes a 2xx; the page never times it out. The bound is the escalation_bound_s column of the alert code in the code table (shared need shared/status-codes.xml#escalation-bound, declared in #shared-needs; default PT24H); the N-31 tick compares open alerts against it every minute and escalates once, so the wait is bounded by the system, never by a person.

retries.s: Client steps retry 3 times with backoff then recover into a visible state (offline, queued ack, 409 shown); nothing loops silently. On the server, alerting is a view, so there is nothing to retry; escalation after the bound is one record and one card.

many-agents.s: Readers: every client sees the same alert view with its own filter; N clients cost N subscriptions, the join is computed once per change.

Two owner devices acknowledging the same alert at once: both send alert.ack with the same version; the store's compare-and-swap lets one write 201 and answers the other 409 with the acker and the time; both rows end identical. No silent overwrite, no double ack.

An ack racing a change: a new attempt record bumps the alert's version; an ack made against the old version gets 409 and the row shows the new system_did, so the owner acknowledges what is there now, not what was.

Many alerts from many seats at once: twenty stalls at once are twenty rows, keyed by alert id (the source record id), never collapsed into a count a seat reports; the system builds at most one card per dead record (N-28 idempotent by source id).

Writes from clients are idempotent by client id and counter; a retried ack (same client id and counter) replays 200 with the earlier result (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys); 409 is only a version conflict.

status-codes.code: Ack recorded against the alert version.
Already acked or the alert changed; the reply names the acker and time; shown, nobody acts.
An open alert passed its escalation bound; one card.
Frame failed schema; full view requested; alert on the transport.
No delta or heartbeat within 10 s.
No view within 10 s; error state, retrying.

look.requirement: owner 04:45Z all views carry the Krastorio look; command-center-visual-bar: the alerts panel reproduced
look.s: The Factorio alert strip and list: rows in a deep frame #242324 with a thin edge, the lamp as a 40 px slot (red #DA4535, amber #FAA838) with original alert pictograms from the atlas (inventory section 5.4: the power bolts are class 1 high; warning triangles and the rest are drawn original until their origin is resolved), the code in mono, the cause in body 14, Open machine as a 108 x 28 tool button, acked rows at the disabled text colour #B3B3B3, the resolved section as a collapsed subheader frame 36 px.
Check: look-check.mjs samples a red row lamp, an amber row lamp, a dimmed acked row and the subheader; binding-check look-token; the screenshot pair read by the architect.

item.check: Alerting is a code property: every red or amber code in the code table appears in the alert view when a record carries it and no later 2xx names it in recovery_of.

item.check: The join fills retries, system_did, card_id and resolved_at from N-11, N-28 and the 2xx record naming the alert in recovery_of.
item.proof: A fixture with a dead ticket after three attempts and a card rendering 3 and the card chip; a fixture where an unrelated 2xx on the same node and ticket leaves the alert open and a 2xx with recovery_of closes it.

item.check: Ack is compare-and-swap on the alert version; a second ack and an ack against a changed alert return 409 with the acker.
item.proof: A test running two acks concurrently and one ack after a version bump.

item.proof: Playwright test asserting the chip count and the lamp after an ack.

item.check: An open alert past its bound produces one 410 alert.aged and one card, never a repeat.
item.proof: A test advancing the clock past the bound twice and counting one card.

permissions.s: Build seat: writes tools/map/src/alerts/**, the Alerts #panels of this volume, and tests; the alert view SQL is a G1 ticket against the Go service (shared need).
Acknowledge requires the owner key; the viewer key sees the control disabled with the reason. No seat acks an alert.

monitoring.s: This screen is the monitor the owner reads; its own health is in frame.report. The map draws N-41 as a machine whose lamp is the latest alerts code; an alert on the transport (422) shows here like any other.

runbook.s: List alerts by hand (reading only): the Go service's gRPC Alerts call, or the dev tier's /events?view=alert (nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views).
Cleanup: acks by N-45 retention; nothing on disk.

sources.src: Screen Alerts: data (alert code from the status code map, node, since, cause line, retry count, what the system did), primary action Jump to the machine.
N-10, N-11, N-12, N-06 records; N-28 one card per dead record.
The board froze six hours and nothing raised it; alerting must be a property of records.
Line 201: the owner, not a check, found the frozen board.
stall, crash, bad-output, governance-interference: detection, recovery, retries 3, then blocked.
No re-confirmation; an ack is one tap and never a required step.

item.reason: an ack that resolves would let the owner silence a fault the system still has; resolution is the system's 2xx
